  How to Submit Public Comment:

  Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the following

  In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit it to the City
  Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes per person per item. At the
  Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the City Council.

  Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as noted below.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 18, 2023
   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, July 18, 2023

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Council Member Ding
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Harrington, Vice Mayor Wu, Council Members Chan, Ding,
  Menchaca

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. AIR QUALITY UPDATE – SOUTH COAST AIR QUALITY MANAGEMENT
  DISTRICT

  B. PRESENTATION TO THE CITY COUNCIL FROM THE SAN GABRIEL K9
  FOUNDATION

  C. PARKS MAKE LIFE BETTER MONTH

  D. RECOGNITION OF OUTSTANDING OLDER AMERICAN – JOSEPH CLARO

  E. DONATION OF ART TO THE SAN GABRIEL FIRE DEPARTMENT – WEST
  CALIFORNIA ART ACADEMY

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of June 20, 2023.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of June 20, 2023.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 18, 2023  2
   Recommended Action: Approval

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – JUNE 2023

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2022-2023 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 22-30) and California Government Code §53646, the
  Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment
  Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s adopted
  2022-2023 Investment Policy.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for June 2023.

  D. RESOLUTION NO. 23-45 APPROVING A THREE-YEAR SERVICE CONTRACT
  IN THE AMOUNT OF $44,299 WITH GOVERNMENTJOBS.COM,
  INCORPORATED FOR WEB-BASED APPLICANT TRACKING, HIRING, AND
  ONBOARDING SERVICES AND INCREASING BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS
  FOR CONTRACTUAL SERVICES

  Governmentjobs.com, Incorporated doing business as NEOGOV, provides the
  paramount Human Resources Management System (HRMS) for public sector
  employee recruitment, hiring, onboarding, development, benefits
  administration, and management. The approval and implementation of

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 18, 2023  3
   NEOGOV will significantly upgrade the City’s employment processing platform
  and improve the employment cycle from initial job advertising through retiree
  benefits administration. Resolution No. 23-45 approves a sole source purchase
  of NEOGOV and increases General Fund appropriations for contractual services.
  The contract with NEOGOV will cost a total of $44,299 over the three-year term.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-45, which
  approves the sole source procurement and three-year contract with NEOGOV,
  increases General Fund appropriations by $9,541 for contractual services, and
  authorizes the City Manager to execute the contract.

  E. FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 FIRE DEPARTMENT SUPPLIES AND EQUIPMENT
  OPEN PURCHASE ORDERS IN THE AMOUNTS OF $65,000 AND $60,000

  The San Gabriel Fire Department, maintains a supply of expendable items and
  durable equipment to fulfil its mission. Open purchase orders, renewed each
  Fiscal Year are used to keep the Department stocked with personal protective
  equipment, paramedic, and firefighting supplies, delivered on an as-needed
  basis. Vendors are reviewed regularly and selected through competitive bid,
  piggyback and cooperative purchasing agreements. Paramedic and Firefighting
  equipment and supplies are budgeted for Fiscal Year 2023-2024 as line items
  in the amount of $75,000 (Emergency Medical Service Supplies) and $70,000
  (Personal Protective Equipment).

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the issuance of open
  purchase orders in the amount of $65,000 to Life Assist, Incorporated and in
  the amount of $60,000 to Municipal Emergency Services. The purchases are to
  be made pursuant to Title III, Section 34.35 of the San Gabriel Municipal Code,
  permitting the City to piggyback on a contract or cooperative purchasing
  agreement prepared by and processed through another local, state, or federal
  government agency.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 18, 2023  4
   F. PURCHASE OF A 2024 RAM 3500 TRUCK FOR THE SAN GABRIEL FIRE
  DEPARTMENT IN THE AMOUNT OF $76,447.23

  The San Gabriel Fire Department is in need of replacing a 1995 Ford F350 Utility
  pickup truck. The purchase was fully funded in the Fiscal Year 2020-2021 Capital
  Improvement Budget, but due to delays in the manufacturing sector, an
  adequate replacement vehicle has not been available for purchase until now.
  The total purchase price, including tax and delivery, is $76,447.23. The
  acquisition of the vehicle is fully funded in account 124-761-15-99-676.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the issuance of a purchase
  order in the amount of $76,447.23 to National Auto Fleet Group for the
  purchase of a 2024 Ram 3500 Tradesman four-wheel pickup truck.

  G. APPROVAL OF PURCHASE ORDER WITH TAYLOR TENNIS COURTS,
  INCORPORATED IN THE AMOUNT OF $35,700 FOR THE RESURFACING OF
  THE TENNIS COURTS AT SMITH PARK AND WASHINGTON SCHOOL PARK

  The existing tennis/pickleball courts at Smith Park and Washington School Park
  are in need of resurfacing. At Smith Park, one court will be striped for tennis
  only and one court for tennis and pickleball. At Washington School Park, both
  courts will be striped for tennis only. The total price for the resurfacing and
  painting of the courts at Smith Park and Washington School Park is $35,700.
  Funds are available in the Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Budget Special Projects
  Account No. 124-850-18-96-816 in the amount of $30,000 for the court
  resurfacing. An appropriation of $9,270 is requested to cover the total amount
  needed for the project. There will be no impact to the General Fund.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Authorize the issuance of a purchase order for $35,700 to Taylor Tennis
  Courts Incorporated for the resurfacing of the courts at Smith Park and
  Washington School Park to be funded from Special Projects Account No.
  124-850-18-96-816.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 18, 2023  5
   2. Authorize the issuance of a separate purchase order for $3,570 to cover a
  10% contingency, if needed, from Special Projects Account No. 124-850-18-
  96-816.
  3. Adopt Resolution No. 23-44 amending the Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Budget to
  appropriate additional funds from the Activities account (Fund 173) to
  Account No. 124-850-18-96-816 for the resurfacing.
  4. Authorize the City Manager to sign the contracts with Taylor Tennis Courts,
  Incorporated.

  H. DECLARATION OF UP TO SIX CAMPING TRAILERS AS SURPLUS PROPERTY
  AND AUTHORIZATION FOR SALE AT AUCTION

  The City of San Gabriel accepted three camping trailers from the Federal
  Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to house infected staff at the start of
  the COVID-19 pandemic. Shortly thereafter, the City accepted five additional
  camping trailers from the City of El Monte, who did not want their FEMA
  allocation of trailers. FEMA provided the titles and keys for all eight trailers, so
  the City is the legal owner of them. The San Gabriel Police Department has been
  using two of the trailers, but the other six have not been used since acquisition
  and staff does not foresee any future need for those camping trailers. The sale
  of said camping trailers is expected to generate between $50,000 and $120,000,
  with the revenue being deposited to the General Fund.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council declare up to six camping trailers as
  surplus property and authorize the City Manager to have them auctioned.

  I. AWARD CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT NO. 23-08 TO COMMERCIAL
  PAVING AND COATING FOR THE CONSTRUCTION OF NEW CONCRETE
  SLAB FOR PICKLEBALL COURTS AT SMITH PARK IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $90,500 PLUS A $9,050 CONTINGENCY

  Smith Park currently has two tennis courts, one of which is striped for both
  tennis and pickleball. The steady increase in popularity of this sport has created
  a need to construct additional pickleball courts. On May 2, 2023, Council
  approved the construction of four new permanent pickleball courts at Smith
  Park. Parks Development Impact Fee funds in the amount of $90,500 plus a
  $9,050 contingency will be utilized to fund the construction of four new

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 18, 2023  6
   pickleball courts. The funds were appropriated in the Fiscal Year 2022-23
  budget and will be carried to the Fiscal Year 2023-24 budget.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Authorize the City Manager to execute Construction Contract No. 23-08
  with Commercial Paving and Construction for a total bid amount of $90,500;
  and
  2. Authorize the City Manager to approve a Purchase Order with Commercial
  Paving and Coating in an amount not to exceed $99,550 which includes a
  10% construction contingency using the Parks Development Impact Fees
  Account No. 122-850-40-97-806.

  J. APPROVAL OF FINAL PARCEL MAP NO. 72302, A 4-UNIT CONDOMINIUM
  DEVELOPMENT PROJECT LOCATED AT 1308 STEVENS AVENUE

  The development project located at 1308 Stevens Avenue, is a 4-unit
  condominium on a 7,249-square-foot lot. Staff and the Los Angeles County
  Department of Public Works have reviewed the Final Parcel Map and
  determined it is in compliance with the State Subdivision Map Act, Conditions
  of Approval, and the City’s ordinances regarding subdivision. There is no fiscal
  impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Final Parcel Map No. 72302,
  authorize its filing with the Los Angeles County Recorder and authorize the City
  Manager to execute the Subdivision Agreement on behalf of the City.

  K. ORDINANCE NO. 690: AMENDING CHAPTER 153 OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO DENSITY BONUS (ZTA23-001) – SECOND
  READING AND ADOPTION

  Adoption of Ordinance No. 690 would amend Title XV, Chapter 153 (Zoning
  Code) of the San Gabriel Municipal Code (SGMC) relating to Density Bonus to
  make it consistent with State law. Ordinance No. 690 was introduced and

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 18, 2023  7
   scheduled for second reading and adoption by a 5-0 vote of the City Council at
  the June 20, 2023, City Council meeting. The Fiscal Year 2022-2023 Adopted
  Budget includes the cost for required legal publication (Account No. 121-702-
  00-65-000) and codification (Account No. 121-702-00-22-000) of the
  ordinance.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive the reading in full, read by title
  only and adopt Ordinance No. 690 entitled, “An Ordinance of the City Council
  of the City of San Gabriel, California, Approving Planning Case No. ZTA23-001,
  Amending Title XV, Chapter 153 (Zoning) relating to Density Bonus.

  L. RESOLUTION NO. 23-43 AMENDING THE AUTHORIZED SCHEDULE OF
  COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS FOR REGULAR NON-REPRESENTED
  EMPLOYEES AND INCREASING BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR REGULAR
  NON-REPRESENTED EMPLOYEE SALARIES AND BENEFITS

  In April, staff began meeting with the Focus Group to discuss the status of the
  Authorized Schedule of Compensation and Benefits (ASCB) for regular non-
  represented employees. Representatives of the City and the Focus Group have
  mutually agreed upon a successor ASCB For Fiscal Year 2023-2024 presented
  for Council’s approval. Resolution No. 23-43 amends the ASCB for all regular
  non-represented employees, effective July 1, 2023.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-43, which
  amends and approves the ASCB for the City’s regular non-represented
  employees for the period covering July 1, 2023, through June 30, 2024, and
  increases General Fund appropriations $508,973 and various other special fund
  appropriations $119,797 to cover increased costs to salaries and benefits for
  the City’s regular non-represented employees.

  M. FIVE YEAR INTERAGENCY COMMUNICATIONS INTEROPERABILITY
  SYSTEM SUBSCRIBER AGREEMENT WITH AN ANNUAL AMOUNT OF
  $11,232

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 18, 2023  8
   As a member of the Verdugo Fire Communications System, the San Gabriel Fire
  Department uses the Interagency Communications Interoperability System (ICI
  System) as the primary radio communications infrastructure for routine and
  emergency response operations. The cost of purchasing, upgrading, and
  maintaining the complex system and mountain top repeater sites is shared
  among the system users. The total cost per year of the ICI Subscriber agreement
  is $11,232.00.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager or designee
  to execute the ICI System Subscriber Agreement and approve the issuance of a
  purchase order in the amount of $11,232 for Fiscal Year 2023-2024.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A. DISCUSSION REGARDING POTENTIAL PROHIBITION OR REGULATIONS
  FOR THE INSTALLATION AND USE OF ARTIFICIAL TURF OR SYNTHETIC
  GRASS ON CITY PARKWAYS

  Current State of California law encourages the use of drought tolerant
  landscaping, including artificial turf or synthetic grass on residential properties.
  Pursuant to the law, cities may adopt laws that provide standards for the type
  and installation of such materials, but may not adopt standards that would
  effectively preclude the use of such materials. State law is silent on the private
  installation of artificial turf on City property, such as a residential parkway.
  Currently, the City of San Gabriel’s Landscape Code only addresses the use of
  artificial or synthetic turf on private property, but not within City owned
  parkways. At the May 16, 2023, City Council meeting, the Council requested that
  staff return with information regarding a potential process to allow artificial turf
  or synthetic grass in the right of way. There is no known fiscal impact for this
  item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 18, 2023  9
   Staff recommends that the City Council discuss the use of artificial turf on city-
  owned parkways, and direct staff to either prohibit the use of these materials
  or amend the standards to allow artificial turf on city-owned parkways. In either
  case, staff will return with a formal Code amendment to implement City
  Council’s direction.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. DISCUSSION AND DIRECTION ON ESTABLISHING A SISTER/FRIENDSHIP
  CITY POLICY AND WHETHER TO CONSIDER ESTABLISHING
  RELATIONSHIPS WITH ADDITIONAL CITIES

  The City of San Gabriel first established a Sister City relationship with the City of
  Celaya, Guanajuato, Mexico in 1967 through the United States/Mexico Sister City
  Association. The City also endorsed a Friendship City with Changhua, Guandong,
  Taiwan through the San Gabriel Chamber of Commerce in 1986. In the past few
  years, City officials have been approached by additional cities with requests to
  establish new Sister City relationships. There is no fiscal impact related to this
  item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council discuss the Sister/Friendship City
  program and provide direction on how to proceed. The following options may
  help to guide the discussion:

  1. Direct staff to return with a policy to guide how the City interacts with the
  current Sister City partners and how to consider future partnerships.
  2. Continue without a formal policy and consider new relationships on an ad
  hoc basis.
  3. Determine that the City should not enter into new relationships at this time.
  4. Any other options that the City Council decides based upon discussion at the
  meeting, including some combination of the options listed above.

  B. COMMUNITY SERVICES  DEPARTMENT  AND  MISSION  PLAYHOUSE
  ANNUAL UPDATE 2023

 8. PUBLIC COMMENT

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 18, 2023  10
   9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The regularly scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday, August 1, 2023 at 6:30

  regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will be available on the Friday

MINUTES OF JULY 18, 2023

I  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Harrington called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
  6:44 P.M. on Tuesday, July 18, 2023, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission
  Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Ding .

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Tony Ding, Denise Menchaca, Vice Mayor
  John Wu, and Mayor John R. Harrington.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith

I  Lemieux, Community Services Director Rebecca Perez,
  Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Publ ic Works Director/City
  Engineer Greg de Vinck, Fire Chief Steven Wallace,
  Human Resources/Risk Management Director Edward
  Macias,  Finance  Director  William  Kaholoku la,
  Community Development Director Aldo Cervantes,
  Interim Police Chief Rikimaru Nakamura, and Assistant
  City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
  how to request meeting agendas.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Chan, to have Presentation Item 2E at about 7:30 P.M.

I  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, MENCHACA, WU, HARRINGTON
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. AIR QUALITY UPDATE -  SOUTH COAST AIR QUALITY MANAGEMENT
  DISTRICT
  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 8  July 18, 2023
   Michael Cacciotti, South Coast AQMD Vice Cha ir made the presentation .

  B. PRESENTATION TO THE CITY COUNCIL FROM THE SAN GABRIEL K9
  FOUNDATION

  Sue Fitzsimmons, President/CEO, Partners with San Gabriel K-9s, made the
  presentation .

I  C. PARKS MAKE LIFE BETTER MONTH

  Community Services Director Perez and Mayor Harrington made the presentation
  and Director Perez accepted the proclamation.

  D. RECOGNITION OF OUTSTANDING OLDER AMERICAN -JOSEPH CLARO

  Community Services Director Perez and Mayor Harrington made the presentation.

  Patty Petevich, on behalf of the Kiwanis Club; Julietta Perez, Executive Director of
  La Casa; Mary Cammarano on behalf of the San Gabriel Historical Association; and
  Cindy Talavera, Kiwanis Advisor, commended Mr. Clara's volunteerism .

  RECESS AND RECONVENE

  The meeting was recessed at 7:19 P.M. and reconvened at 7:33 P.M. with all Council

  E. DONATION OF ART TO THE SAN GABRIEL FIRE DEPARTMENT - WEST

I  CALIFORNIA ART ACADEMY
  Lei Wang, Principal of the West Cal ifornia Art Academy in San Gabriel, and students
  Al isa Chang and Eric Chang made the presentation, Fire Chief Wallace accepted on
  beha lf of the Fi re Department, and Mayor Harrington presented Certificates of
  Recognition to students Eric Chang, Alisa Chang, and Victoria Wang .

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Former Council Member Carina Rivera, resident, provided comments wishing Vice
  Mayor Wu a happy birthday.

  Andrew, resident, commented on his opposition to the City Attorney prosecuting
  misdemeanor crimes, commended Police Sergeant Nhat Huynh fo r working for
  change, and Menta l Evaluation Team Pol ice Officer Cecily Ramirez for developing a
  youth leadership academy for youth aged 12-17 years and suggested that other
  department directo rs develop a training for youth.

  Mary Garcia, resident, expressed dissatisfaction with overgrown vegetation at the

I  freeway underpass and offramp at San Gabriel Boulevard, and at res idences in the City.

  Chasity Nunez, resident, spoke in opposition to the City purchasing a San Gabriel
  Chamber of Commerce membership or giving the Chamber a grant and suggested
  there are better ways to spend the money.

  Victor Gau, Secretary, I-Chinese American Political Action Committee; Robert Liu,
  President, of Chinese American Education Association, and Wei Sun, President, U.S. -
  China Economic Trade and Cultural Arts Federation, expressed support and
  congratulations to Lei Wang and the West California Art Academy's presentation of
  art to the San Gabriel Fire Department.
  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 8  July 18, 2023
   4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  Chief City Clerk Clark announced that requests to pull items 4H and 41 for separate
  consideration had been received from the public, and that pursuant to Government
  Code §54953(c)(3) reporting requirements, Consent Item 4L included the following
  benefit changes for all regular non-represented employees including executive
  management as follows:

I  •

  •
  5% base salary increase effective the pay period beginning July 1, 2023 . This
